supported_claims.text: The dossier supports a pictographic analysis of 用 as a bucket or container with a body on the left and handle on the right. This is an attributed paleographic interpretation, not a directly inspected image.

Oracle-bone examples are reported for 用/不用 in contexts indicating whether a proposed action was carried out. This supports an early attested use for ‘carry out/use’, but does not establish that use as the graph’s original meaning or its priority over a proposed container sense.

The graph is reported in bronze inscriptions with verb, prepositional, and conjunctive uses. A Qin-slip example is read 桶 in a measure or container context, but these examples do not establish a complete chronology.
A catalogue indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script, and 說文 forms of 用, but its accessible text does not describe individual strokes or date a first occurrence.

disagreements.text: The bucket-and-handle pictograph analysis conflicts with the received 說文 structural account 從卜從中. A separate report describes 用 and 同 as graphic variants or a divided graph; the dossier’s Wiktionary excerpt instead analyzes 用 as 同 plus a handle, with 同 phonetic. The inspected evidence does not adjudicate these accounts or establish 同 as a phonetic component.

limitations.text: The bucket/container interpretation is a reported scholarly analysis; no oracle-bone facsimile was independently inspected, and the dossier does not identify the pictured object’s spoken name. The proposed borrowing of the graph for ‘put into effect/use’ therefore lacks an independently established sound match.
The earliest occurrence and relative chronology of the proposed container sense and the attested ‘carry out/use’ sense remain unresolved. The Qin-slip 桶 reading does not settle their order.

用’s supplied Middle Chinese and Old Chinese readings are readings of 用 itself, not evidence for an internal phonetic component or for the sound of the pictured object. No component sound comparison is supported.
No selected historical glyph image is available in the dossier; the form catalogue lacks a described stroke analysis, and the surfaced seal-script image’s provenance and permission were not verified.
